description: Chain ops in one call: each step is {op, input?, args?, as?, input_type?}, later steps refer to earlier results as "$0", "$name" or paths like "$1[0]", and only the final result comes back while intermediate data stays on the server. Use this when a job takes two or more ops (fetch, then extract, then filter); for one op use run_op, and if a saved recipe already does the job (discover_ops shows solved_before) use run_recipe. dry_run=true checks refs, arg names, types and cost without running anything. Up to 50 steps. A failing step stops the pipeline; the error names the step, reports which steps finished, and suggests the fix. Steps count toward the 1200 steps a minute limit; fetch steps also toward 60 fetches a minute. Example steps: [{"op": "fetch", "args": {"url": "https://example.com/pricing"}, "as": "page"}, {"op": "extract_tables", "input": "$page", "args": {"index": 0}}, {"op": "to_markdown", "input": "$1"}].

args.description: The op's arguments; values may be refs.

as.description: Name this step so later steps can use "$name".

input.description: A ref ("$0", "$page", "$1[0]", "$2.items[*].name"), a handle id, or a literal.

input_type.description: Override the type of a literal input.

inline_max_tokens.description: Return the value itself when it's at most this many estimated tokens, else a preview. Default 300.

result_from.description: Which step to return, as a ref like "$2" or "$prices[0]". Default: the last step.

steps.description: Ordered steps, 1 to 50. A literal string starting with $ is written $$.

terse.description: Return only the answer (value, or handle and preview), without steps, hashes or hints.

name: run_pipeline

handle.description: terse, large result: its handle id.

problems.description: dry_run: what would fail, per step.

result.description: The returned step's handle, as in run_op.

steps.description: Per step: op, handle, type, est_tokens, ms.

totals.description: dry_run: the estimate: steps, cost, side effects (e.g. reads_network), deterministic.
